keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria has no Celtiberian row; the page has no infobox area. Celtiberia (Soria, Guadalajara, Zaragoza, Teruel) in the gazetteer; the Ebro divides it from the non-Indo-European peoples. Soft edges.

correction.text: Celtiberia without the Zaragoza province (the Ebro side), the part the Romans took in 195: 'In 195 BC, part of Celtiberia was conquered by the Romans' (the page does not say which part)

keyframe_review.note: After Cato's consulship (195) the Ebro side is Roman. Which part of Celtiberia fell is not on the Celtiberians page ('part of Celtiberia was conquered') nor on the Cato the Elder page, which says only that Cato 'reduced Hispania Citerior to subjection' and 'the area between the River Iberus and the Pyrenees' (195-194); Zaragoza province, the Ebro-side part of the Celtiberian provinces, is the researcher's reading (confidence 2 on the loss). The shape holds to Numantia's fall in 133.

region.text: Celtiberia: the Arevaci, Belli, Titti and Lusones

ledger.note: c. 500 BC: the Celtiberians' 'cultural stronghold in the northern central meseta, in the upper Tagus and Douro valleys east to the Ebro, in the modern provinces of Soria, Guadalajara, Zaragoza, and Teruel'; tribes Arevaci (Okilis), Belli and Titti (Jalon), Lusones, Pellendones; towns Numantia, Segeda, Termantia, Kontebakom-Bel. No formation date on the page; 500 is a placeholder.

region.text: the middle Ebro, the eastern edge of Celtiberia

ledger.note: 195 BC: 'part of Celtiberia was conquered in 195 BC' (Cato); uprising 195-193. Which part is the researcher's reading: the Cato the Elder page (opened 2026-10-19) speaks of Hispania Citerior reduced 'to subjection' in 195-194 and of 'the area between the River Iberus and the Pyrenees', and names no Celtiberian town; Zaragoza province is the Ebro-side part of Celtiberia.
